environment.description: Same NestJS service deployed behind AWS API Gateway HTTP API with a Lambda authorizer that performs tenant-scoped resource resolution. The authorizer extracts the JWT subject claim, queries DynamoDB tenant-resource-mapping table (partition key: resourceId, sort key: tenantId), and returns an IAM policy with explicit Deny on execute-api:Invoke if the resource's tenantId does not match the caller's tenant claim. Additionally, the API Gateway route configuration uses request parameter mapping to inject x-tenant-boundary header derived from the authorizer context, and the ALB target group has a listener rule condition requiring this header to match a regex pattern ^tenant-[a-f0-9]{8}$ before forwarding. The SRI hashes on script tags ensure that even if an attacker attempts to serve modified viewer JavaScript (e.g., via a compromised CDN or cache poisoning) to exfiltrate document data client-side, the browser will refuse to execute scripts whose content doesn't match the pinned sha384 digests. CloudFront distribution serving /assets/* has Origin Access Identity with read-only on a versioned S3 bucket with Object Lock in compliance mode.

config.api_gateway: HTTP API with Lambda authorizer performing tenant-resource DynamoDB lookup
config.authorizer_logic: Returns explicit Deny IAM policy when DynamoDB query for (resourceId=documentId, tenantId=caller.tenantId) returns empty
config.alb_header_validation: Listener rule requires x-tenant-boundary header matching ^tenant-[a-f0-9]{8}$
config.sri: sha384 integrity attributes on all external script references
config.cdn: CloudFront with OAI, versioned S3 with Object Lock compliance mode
